extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, patent attorneys and agents, and USPTO filing staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements from the MPEP/CFR governing fees, payment methods, deposit accounts, refunds, small-entity status, and formatting/fee consequences for reexamination and supplemental proceedings. Includes specific fee amounts, timing, and procedural prerequisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issuance fee for certificate of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: For providing a certificate of correction for an applicant’s mistake (§ 1.323): $172.00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing fee for correcting inventorship in a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing fee for correcting inventorship in a patent (§ 1.324): $172.00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting requirements for ex parte reexamination request to qualify for standard fee tier
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte reexamination request (§ 1.510(a)) having 40 or fewer pages; lines that are double-spaced or one-and-a-half spaced; text written in a non-script type font such as Arial, Times New Roman, or Courier; and contrast to permit direct reproduction and electronic capture by use of digital imaging and optical character recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such conforming requests fall under a specific fee table (TABLE 1 TO PARAGRAPH (c)(1)(i)). Font, spacing, page count, and OCR-compatibility are required to obtain the reduced fee tier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts excluded from reexamination formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of every patent or printed publication relied upon in the request (§ 1.510(b)(3)); copy of the entire patent for which reexamination is requested (§ 1.510(b)(4)); and certifications required pursuant to § 1.510(b)(5) and (6) are excluded from the page/formatting limits in paragraphs (c)(1)(i)(A)-(F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These excluded parts need not meet the 40-page/spacing/font/contrast requirements for the reduced-fee tier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for filing ex parte reexamination requests (by entity type / by conformity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee tables differentiate amounts by micro entity, small entity, and other than small/micro entity for different filing scenarios (e.g., conforming requests under (c)(1)(i) vs. requests under (c)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the chunk: TABLE 1 TO PARAGRAPH (c)(1)(i) lists $1,355 (micro), $2,710 (small), $6,775 (other). TABLE 2 TO PARAGRAPH (c)(2) lists $2,709 (micro), $5,418 (small), $13,545 (other). (Full fee tables in the regulation should be consulted for precise current amounts and contexts.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for each independent claim in excess of three (and in excess of claims in patent under reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: For filing with a request for reexamination or later presentation of each claim in independent form in excess of three and also in excess of the number of claims in independent form in the patent under reexamination, an excess-claim fee applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting requirements referenced near this provision: font size no smaller than 12 point, margins conforming to § 1.52(a)(1)(ii), and sufficient clarity/contrast for OCR. TABLE 3 TO PARAGRAPH (c)(3) and TABLE 4 TO PARAGRAPH (c)(4) give per-claim amounts by entity type (examples elsewhere in the section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for filing each claim in excess of 20 (and excess of claims in patent under reexamination)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee applies for filing with a request for reexamination or later presentation at any time of each claim (dependent or independent) in excess of 20 and also in excess of the number of claims in the patent under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TABLE 4 TO PARAGRAPH (c)(4) provides per-claim fees by entity type (examples: $40 micro, $80 small, $200 other). See § 1.75(c) for treatment of multiple dependent claims for fee calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement for excess-claim fees or cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the excess-claims fees required by paragraphs (c)(3) and (c)(4) are not paid with the request for reexamination or on later presentation of the claims for which the excess-claims fees are due, the fees must be paid or the claims canceled by amendment prior to the expiration of the time period set for reply by the Office in any notice of fee deficiency to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely pay excess-claim fees or cancel the excess claims will lead to abandonment consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for refused ex parte reexamination request (already included in filing fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee for a refused request for ex parte reexamination under § 1.510 is included in the request-for-ex-parte-reexamination fee at § 1.20(c)(1) or (2). Separate table (TABLE 6 TO PARAGRAPH (c)(7)) lists amounts by entity type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples shown in the chunk: TABLE 6 lists $756 (micro), $1,512 (small), $3,780 (other). Consult full regulation for the current applicable values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees and timing (patents based on applications filed on/after Dec 12, 1980)
rubrics_metrics.description: For maintaining an original or any reissue patent (except design or plant) in force beyond specified years, maintenance fees are due at specific times: beyond four years (due by 3.5 years after grant), beyond eight years (due by 7.5 years), and beyond twelve years (due by 11.5 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate fee tables (TABLE 7, TABLE 8, TABLE 9) list amounts by micro, small, and other than small or micro entities (examples in chunk include amounts such as $430/$860/$2,150 for the 3.5-year fee (TABLE 7), $1,656/$3,312/$8,280 for the 7.5-year fee (TABLE 8), and $439/$878/$2,195 for 11.5-year fee (TABLE 9)). Surcharges apply for payment during the six-month grace period (TABLE 10 lists $108/$216/$540).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharge for paying maintenance fee during six-month grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: A surcharge is imposed for paying a maintenance fee during the six-month grace period following the expiration of maintenance-fee deadlines (3.5, 7.5, and 11.5 years after grant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TABLE 10 provides surcharge amounts by entity type (examples: $108 micro, $216 small, $540 other).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for applications to extend patent term and interim extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for filing an application for extension of the term of a patent: application for extension under § 1.740: $2,500.00; initial application for interim extension under § 1.790: $1,320.00; subsequent application for interim extension under § 1.790: $680.00; requesting supplemental redetermination after notice of final determination: $1,440.00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in supplemental examination and related reexamination outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees apply for processing and treating a request for supplemental examination and for ex parte reexamination ordered as a result of supplemental examination. Fees differ by entity type and by the action ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: TABLE 8 TO PARAGRAPH (k)(1) lists processing fees for supplemental examination (e.g., $808 micro, $1,616 small, $4,040 other). TABLE 12 TO PARAGRAPH (k)(2) lists fees for ex parte reexamination ordered as a result of supplemental examination (e.g., $2,731 micro, $5,462 small, $13,655 other). Additional per-document processing fees apply for non-patent documents over 20 sheets (TABLE 13 and TABLE 14 provide per-document amounts by entity and sheet counts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory disclaimer filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: For filing each statutory disclaimer (§ 1.321): $183.00.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and discipline-related fees for attorneys and agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for registration to practice (application fee non-refundable $118), registration examination fees (commercial test administration $226), USPTO-administered review of registration examination $505, request for extension to schedule exam $124, fee on registration to practice $226, fee on grant of limited recognition $226, certificates of good standing ($43 standard, $54 suitable for framing), review of decisions by Director of Enrollment and Discipline $452, administrative reinstatement fees (delinquency $54; reinstatement $226), and fee for recognition/registration after disbarment or similar events $1,806.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some items reserved; consult full section for complete list and current amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit account establishment and minimum funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit accounts may be established for convenience upon payment of the fee for establishing a deposit account. A minimum deposit of $1,000 is required for paying any fee due or ordering Office services; a restricted subscription deposit account used exclusively for subscription order of patent copies may be established with a minimum deposit of $300.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the end of each month a statement is rendered; the account holder must promptly remit to restore the account to its normal deposit. Amounts sufficient to cover requested items must always be on deposit; charges to accounts with insufficient funds will not be accepted. Service charges apply if balance falls below thresholds (§ 1.21(b)(2)-(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorizations to charge deposit accounts and effect on payment date
rubrics_metrics.description: A general authorization to charge fees to a deposit account may be filed in an individual application for the entire pendency or for a particular paper; authorizations to charge for various specific proceedings (reexamination, supplemental examination, international design transmittal, etc.) may be filed with the request. An authorization to charge a fee to a deposit account will not be considered payment on the date the authorization is effective unless sufficient funds are present in the account to cover the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific authorizations have applicability limits (e.g., certain international transmittal fees) and are subject to provisions of other sections (e.g., § 1.311(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of payment and permitted instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: All payments of money required for USPTO fees shall be made in U.S. dollars and in the form of a cashier’s or certified check, Treasury note, national bank notes, or United States Postal Service money order. Payments from foreign countries must be payable and immediately negotiable in the U.S. for the full amount. Checks and money orders must be payable to the Director of the USPTO (checks payable to the Commissioner will continue to be accepted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sent in other forms, the Office may delay or cancel credit until collection is made. Money sent by mail is at sender's risk; letters containing money should be registered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit card payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments may be made by credit card except for replenishing a deposit account. Payment by credit card must specify the amount to be charged and necessary information to process the charge; the Office will not accept a general authorization to charge a credit card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If credit card information is provided on a form or document other than an Office-provided form for credit-card payment, the Office will not be liable if the credit-card number becomes public knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees payable in advance and itemization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees and charges payable to the USPTO are required to be paid in advance at the time of requesting any action for which a fee is payable, except that applications may be assigned a filing date without payment of the basic filing fee under § 1.53. All fees paid must be itemized in each individual application, patent, or proceeding so it is clear for which purpose the fees are paid; the Office may return fees not itemized as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provisions of § 1.5(a) do not apply to resubmission of fees returned for lack of itemization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund policy and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may refund any fee paid by mistake or in excess. A change of purpose after payment (e.g., withdrawal of filing) will not entitle a party to a refund. The Office will not refund amounts of $25 or less unless a refund is specifically requested. Any refund request generally must be filed within two years from date the fee was paid (with some exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If payor does not provide banking information for EFT refunds or request credit to a deposit account, the Director may require such information or use banking information on the payment instrument. Credit-card refunds will be credited to the card account charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds specific to reexamination and supplemental examination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director decides not to institute reexamination or supplemental examination, certain fees paid with the request will be refunded: for an ex parte reexamination request, the filing fee less the fee set in § 1.20(c)(7) will be refunded; for an inter partes reexamination request, a refund of $7,970 will be made if not instituted; for supplemental examination, the fee for reexamination ordered as a result of supplemental examination (§ 1.20(k)(2)) will be returned if no reexamination is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requester or patent owner should indicate the form of refund (check, EFT, credit to deposit account). Generally refunds will be issued in the form of the original payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and criteria for 'small entity' status
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'small entity' as used in this chapter means any party qualifying under the person, small business concern, or nonprofit organization paragraphs. A 'person' is an inventor or other individual who has not assigned, licensed, or is under obligation to assign rights in the invention; a small business concern must meet the size standards in 13 CFR 121.801–121.805 and not have assigned/licensed rights to entities that would not qualify; a nonprofit organization must meet requirements including being a university, a 26 U.S.C. 501(c)(3) organization, certain nonprofit scientific/educational organizations, or a foreign nonprofit that would qualify if located in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rights have been transferred, all parties holding rights must qualify for small-entity status for the applicant to qualify. Contact SBA Size Standards Staff for small-business questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Government use license exceptions to small-entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Claiming small-entity status is not prohibited for persons in an application filed/prosecuted/maintained at no expense to the Government where certain Government use licenses result from Executive Order 10096 or other federal agency action (e.g., 15 U.S.C. 3710d(a) circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section enumerates specific Government-license-derived exceptions that do not bar small-entity status for persons under paragraph (a)(1). Consult the complete section for detailed conditions and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for recording assignments and related papers
rubrics_metrics.description: For recording each assignment, agreement, or other paper relating to the property in a patent or application, per property: if submitted electronically on or after Jan. 1, 2014: $0.00; if not submitted electronically: $54.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submission after the specified date avoids the per-property fee; check current procedures for acceptable electronic formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous small fees and service charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Various smaller fees and service charges are prescribed: service charge for each month when deposit-account balance is below $1,000: $25.00; service charge for restricted subscription accounts below $300: $25.00; processing each payment refused or charged back: $50.00; handling an application where proceedings are terminated pursuant to § 1.53(e): $151.00; Official Gazette publication fee per application/patent: $27.00; international type search report preparation: $43.00; additional fee for overnight delivery: $43.00; additional fee for expedited service: $183.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some items are marked [Reserved] or subject to change. Consult the full regulation section for the precise current list and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mega-sequence listing fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt of a very lengthy sequence listing (mega-sequence listing) in an application under 35 U.S.C. 111 or 371 is subject to fees: first receipt of a sequence listing in electronic form 300MB–800MB (without compression): TABLE 1 lists amounts by entity; exceeding 800MB: TABLE 2 lists larger amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the chunk: for 300–800MB TABLE 1 shows $228 micro, $456 small, $1,140 other; for >800MB TABLE 2 shows $2,258 micro, $4,516 small, $11,290 other. Confirm current thresholds and amounts in CFR.
